Senses.Explanation: This interrogative asks how something is, how one will respond, or what can be said or done: “how?” Its force is often a live demand rather than a request for exposition. Baizhang Huaihai blocks throat and lips and asks how Guishan will speak; Shitou Xiqian rejects “this way” and “not this way” and asks what his student will do; Linji Yixuan asks how the present listener proposes to cultivate, realize, or adorn the person hearing the teaching. It also follows a proposed action—“what if the foot is raised?”—asks how someone understands a case, presses “ultimately, how?”, asks how a ceremonial address should be raised, or introduces “what is the final phrase?” Dialectal spellings perform the same interrogative work in the cited passages. The phrase supplies no answer by itself; its recurring role is to force the next move.

Senses.Explanation: How do you understand it? A recurrent public-interview question put to an individual or the whole assembly after a saying, action, quotation, or case has been raised. Linji Yixuan asks how an unnamed participant understands the four stated uses of a shout and answers the participant’s hesitation with a shout. Wufeng Ziqi asks, ‘How do you understand it?’ (你作麼生會); the unnamed respondent shouts, and Wufeng says ‘not yet’ (未在) before asking what comes after one shout or two. In a whisk case, Ganzi Xingzhe asks how a visitor understands Guishan Lingyou’s intention in raising the whisk; the offered account is rejected with ‘You had better return to Guishan’ (且歸溈山去好). Cuiyan Shouzhi says that National Teacher Huizhong and his attendant both still lacked understanding and asks, ‘How do you understand it now?’ (如今作麼生會). Yunju Shun similarly reopens the Puyan–Samantabhadra case for the assembly. The phrase demands an answer that can itself be answered, rejected, or tested in public; the texts do not define it as silent inward comprehension.

Senses.Explanation: To calculate and guess; speculative reckoning. The graphs join ‘divine or forecast’ (卜) to ‘measure or estimate’ (度). The compound has 778 occurrences in 227 storage files. Its recurrent coordinations locate the act in thinking, affective cognition, the root of thought, and mental weighing without creating additional senses. Dahui Zonggao says, in a list, ‘do not reckon under the root of thought; do not give a phrase; do not remain silent for a long time’ (不得向意根下卜度，不得下語，不得良久). His memorial inscription says, ‘Chan, Chan: do not use thinking and conjectural calculation; it does not concern written words and speech’ (禪禪不用思量卜度，非干文字語言). Yuanwu Keqin asks in the Blue Cliff Record whether the cited matter can be reckoned by affective cognition (以情識卜度得麼). Baoguo Zhao warns the assembly not to conjecture inside cognition because that becomes inverted imagining (莫向意識裏卜度，却成妄想顛倒). Shaoshan Daoxin gives the compact public-interview verdict: ‘if you conjecture, you lose body and life’ (卜度則喪身失命). Zen bends an ordinary term for divinatory estimation into a recurrent name for the mental guessing explicitly rejected at the teaching seat. Yongjue Yuanxian says that conjecturing within discriminating consciousness leaves only a vaguely perceived clod; Shending Yunwai Ze groups conjecture and discursive thought with outward seeking and self-binding. Both confirm the same act of speculative assessment.

Senses.Explanation: The compound judges a person, answer, explanation, or speech as fabricated and also serves as a verb for making such material up. Jiexian criticizes assigning difficult cases to newcomers without matching the person and the case: after comparing it to fitting a square timber into a round hole and losing people's time, Jiexian says, 'To call it fabricated—is that not fitting?' (謂之杜撰，不亦宜乎). A playful assembly exchange separates the graphs as a surname and personal name: the staff says, 'My surname is Du, given name Zhuan'; asked why it is called 'fabricated,' it answers, 'If the elder did not fabricate, how could he spend all day talking about Zhang and Li?' (長老若不杜撰，如何終日與人說張說李). Dahui uses the word self-deprecatingly when he says, 'I have not read Guo Xiang's explanation or the various commentators' explanations; I only rely on my own fabrication to explain your silence' (我也不曾看郭象解并諸家注解，只據我杜撰說破爾這默然). The stock rebuke 'fabricated elder' (杜撰長老) is attested, often in the fuller comparison 'fabricated elders are like hemp and millet'—that is, extremely numerous (杜撰長老如麻似粟). 'Fabricated Zen fellow' (杜撰禪和) likewise appears as a verdict on a respondent, while 'fabricated conjectural talk' (杜撰臆說) names speech. All of these are uses of the same judgment: the wording or the person’s handling is made up rather than grounded.
